commitResults.messageBody:
The app needs to represent classes so students can later be assigned to
or removed from them.

The MVP specifies that each class is identified by a module code and
class name pair. The model should enforce that identity before command,
storage, or UI work builds on top of it.

Let's add academic class model classes for module code, class name, and
student membership.

The value objects normalize stored values to uppercase and validate the
input rules from the MVP. The academic class model follows the existing
Person model style, including immutable fields, identity comparison,
equality, hashing, and string formatting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align academic class equality with identity
commitResults.messageBody:
AcademicClass has no planned need for equality that includes student
membership.

Including students in equals makes duplicate checks and collection use
depend on assignment state, even though the MVP identifies a class by its
module code and class name pair.

Let's make AcademicClass equality use only module code and class name.

This keeps equals consistent with the class identity rule used by future
add, delete, list, assign, and unassign features.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicate academic class identity method
commitResults.messageBody:
AcademicClass uses module code and class name as its equality rule.

The separate identity helper has the same behavior as equals, so keeping
both methods creates an unnecessary second API for future class features.

Let's remove the duplicate identity helper and keep equals as the single
comparison method.

This keeps the model simpler while preserving the MVP identity rule for
academic classes.

The app needs to store academic classes before create, delete, list,
assign, and unassign commands can work reliably.

Academic classes are uniquely identified by their module code and class
name pair. This identity rule needs to be enforced at the model level so
future features use the same duplicate handling.

Let's add a uniqueness-enforcing academic class list to AddressBook and
include academic classes in JSON storage.

This keeps class data managed alongside persons while preserving
insertion order for future listclass behavior.

Users need a command to create classes that students can later be
assigned to.

The MVP requires addclass to accept module code and class name in any
order, reject missing or repeated parameters, normalize values, and
prevent duplicate module-code/class-name pairs.

Let's add the addclass command, parser, CLI prefixes, and parser helpers
for academic class fields.

This implements the command behavior while reusing the model's academic
class identity and validation rules.

Created classes need to appear immediately after a successful addclass
command.

The model exposes academic classes as an observable list, but the UI
does not have a panel that displays that list.

Let's add an academic class list panel and card, then wire it into the
main window through Logic.

This keeps the UI update path consistent with the existing person list
panel while showing classes in insertion order.

The rebased addclass branch should follow the project's Java coding
standard before opening the pull request.

Some touched files had minor Javadoc formatting gaps and an extra blank
line that Checkstyle did not flag directly.

Let's add the missing public constructor documentation, format the model
API comment consistently, and clean up parser and model whitespace.

The addclass PR has uncovered model, logic, and storage paths in the
academic class workflow.

Let's add focused tests for academic class list access, duplicate class
handling, model manager delegation, logic list exposure, and JSON class
serialization.

This also updates the section labels to use white text so Students and
Classes remain readable on the dark background.

Codecov still reports missing lines in the academic class UI and JSON
adapter changes.

Let's add focused JavaFX tests for the academic class card, list panel,
and main window wiring, plus the remaining empty-field JSON adapter
cases.

This covers the source lines added for displaying academic classes while
keeping the tests scoped to the new UI components.

The addclass command and parser comments should describe the current
behavior in plain language.

Let's tighten the wording without changing command behavior so the PR
can retrigger CI with a small documentation-only update.

The new academic class UI tests start the JavaFX toolkit, which needs a
display on the Ubuntu GitHub runner.

Run the Linux Gradle check through xvfb-run so JavaFX has a virtual
display in CI while keeping the normal command for macOS and Windows.
Support alphabetical filtered person views

The class list should show each class as a combined module and class
name, with the second row reserved for assignment status.

Let's display classes as '<module code> <class name>' and replace the
module row with the current number of students assigned to the class.

This also points the help window to the team User Guide instead of the
original AB3 guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update user guide for MVP features
commitResults.messageBody:
Document the implemented student and class commands against the current codebase.

Also call out specified MVP commands that are not yet available in this build, so users are not given unsupported command words.

Update the guide title and product description to match the NUS Teaching Assistant user profile.

Replace remaining ClassConnect references in the guide with TAssist so the documentation uses one product name consistently.
Update Class UI and User Guide for MVP Features
Update Assign Student to Class documentation

commitResults.messageTitle: List classes by displayed student index
commitResults.messageBody:
Students can be assigned to several classes, but their memberships
cannot be listed directly from the displayed student list.

Add listbystudent INDEX to show the selected student's classes in
creation order while preserving the student view and stored data.

Refresh the class filter after membership changes, student edits,
and student deletion. Keep listclass as the way to restore all classes.

Validate indexes with exceptions, check the filter postcondition with
an assertion, and log diagnostic events at FINE level. Cover filtering,
invalid input, live updates, and restart persistence with tests.

Gradle application runs do not explicitly enable assertions, so
internal invariant checks can be skipped during manual testing.

Enable assertions for Gradle run and test tasks. Add a shared IntelliJ
configuration that delegates to Gradle so developers use the same
assertion settings.

Document assertion flags for direct IDEA and JAR execution, and align
the setup guide with the Java 25 build requirement.

Teaching assistants need to understand which student index to use
and why unrelated classes disappear from the filtered class panel.

Document listbystudent with setup commands, expected results, empty
memberships, invalid input, and live updates. Explain how list and
listclass restore the two views independently.

Update the README and manual testing instructions, and correct obsolete
notes about class listing and membership updates.

The developer guide omits the addclass command flow and academic class
relationships in the model diagram.

Add the AddClass sequence diagram and show academic classes, their
identity fields, and student membership in the model diagram. Explain
the command flow in the guide to keep the documentation aligned with
the implementation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split AddClass sequence into component views
commitResults.messageBody:
The AddClass diagram mixes parsing details, object creation, and model
interaction in one wide sequence. The reference undo/redo feature uses
separate Logic and Model views to explain component responsibilities.

Simplify the Logic sequence and add a Model sequence that expands class
list updates and observer registration. Restructure the feature guide
around the example steps and document the omitted calls and failures.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reset class filter when replacing address book
commitResults.messageBody:
The selected student's class filter survives address book replacement.
After listbystudent, clearing the data and adding a class leaves the
new class hidden because it has no membership for the previous student.

Reset the class view through the existing filter update method when
replacing the address book. Clear the selected student and saved
predicate together so membership changes cannot restore the old filter.

Add regression tests for listbystudent followed by clear and addclass,
and for data replacement followed by membership changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge remote updates into student class listing
commitResults.messageBody:
The remote feature branch includes the latest master changes while
the local branch adds the class filter reset and regression tests.

Combine both histories and retain the student and class view resets
when replacing the address book so clearing data resets both filters.

The diagrams lack named sequence frames and explicit many-to-many
student membership. Destruction markers imply object disposal that the
implementation does not perform, and duplicate rejection is only prose.

Add sequence frames, show membership multiplicities at both ends, and
replace destruction markers with activation endings. Show duplicate
rejection in an alternative fragment and align the guide with the
revised diagrams.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test class edits during student class lookup
commitResults.messageBody:
Student class lookup and class editing work together, but their
interaction with later assignments lacks integration coverage.

Add a regression test for listbystudent followed by editclass and
assignment changes. Verify the view uses the edited class instance,
preserves memberships, and rejects assignments to the old identity.

Check that unassigning and reassigning the selected student hides and
restores the edited class so stale references cannot pass unnoticed.
Add logging to deleting a class

Class lookup logs its result, but model updates provide no diagnostic
trace of filter resets, refreshes, or membership changes.

Add FINE logging for class filter selection and refreshes, assignments,
unassignments, and address book replacement. Include the student number
in lookup results and log changes to the selected student's number.

Keep these diagnostics at FINE level to support debugging without
adding noise to normal application logs.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refresh the workspace layout and theme
commitResults.messageBody:
The vertically stacked class and student lists limit the space available
to inspect both, and inconsistent styling makes the interface harder to
scan.

Arrange classes and students in an adjustable split below the command
input and output. Show passive, wrapping class rows and apply a shared
slate-blue theme with clearer keyboard focus indicators, including Help.

Reuse the scoped layout and palette from refresh-ui while keeping
command execution, filtering and attendance presentation unchanged.
Cover class row wrapping and read-only list behaviour with regression
tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Compact student cards and wrap long details
commitResults.messageBody:
Student cards reserve unnecessary vertical space, while long contact
details can become unreadable in a narrow student panel.

Compact the cards and let names, contacts and tags wrap within their
available width. Reserve enough height for wrapped flow-pane labels and
retain the existing attendance label and date formatting.

Add card and assembled-workspace regression tests to verify resizing,
passive class rows, executed-command filters and attendance updates.
Check that typing alone leaves the displayed data unchanged.

Reviewers need repeatable checks for the layout refresh without changing
their normal application data or relying on features from other
branches.

Add Markdown and plain-text instructions for this branch's layout,
theme, filtering and attendance regression checks. Provide an isolated
demo launcher with separate data and preferences so the setup can be
repeated safely.

The Classes list disables keyboard focus and row selection, preventing
keyboard users from inspecting classes below the visible area.

Restore Tab access with a focusable read-only list and a visible focus
border. Reuse JavaFX scrolling for arrow, page and boundary keys while
keeping class rows unselected and displayed data unchanged.

Add regression coverage for focus traversal, scrolling, boundaries and
empty lists. Update both manual testing guides with keyboard checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover read-only list shortcuts and skin cleanup
commitResults.messageBody:
Keyboard scrolling tests leave shortcut handling and skin disposal
unverified. Regressions could intercept modified keys or leave an old
scrolling handler active after a skin is replaced.

Add focused tests for Alt, Control and Meta modifiers, handler cleanup
and restored scrolling after skin replacement. Close the coverage gaps
while keeping production behaviour unchanged.
Prevent multiple application from launching

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle scrolling keys in empty class lists
commitResults.messageBody:
When Classes is empty, scrolling keys fall through to JavaFX 17
selection handlers. Home and End then dereference the disabled selection
model and throw an exception.

Consume scrolling keys when no cell is visible while preserving focus
traversal and Help accelerators. Keep the list read-only without
invoking selection behaviour.

Add an empty-list regression test that verifies key consumption before
default handling, including on newer runtimes that mask the crash.
Extend both manual guides with the empty-list checks.
Update application's icon and name

commitResults.messageTitle: Align the workspace test with the app title
commitResults.messageBody:
The merge from master renames the window to TAssist App, but the
workspace test still expects TAssist. This mismatch fails the test after
the branding change.

Update the expected title to match the merged application branding so
the layout regression check passes without reverting the team change.
Refresh TAssist layout and visual styling

commitResults.messageTitle: Add live workspace feedback and class navigation
commitResults.messageBody:
Filtered class and student lists provide no live counts or explicit
empty states. Successful class-index commands can leave the affected
class outside the visible area, and saved windows can restore below the
workspace's intended minimum size.

Add observable header counts, empty messages and class scrolling after
successful commands. Enforce the requested 720 by 600 minimum on
restored windows while preserving command execution, filtering and
attendance.

Cover data changes, zero results, filtered targets and window
restoration with UI regression tests. Keep class rows passive and input
drafts inert.

The usability changes need repeatable manual checks without modifying
normal application data or the layout branch's demo session.

Add Markdown and plain-text guides for counts, empty states, class
scrolling and restored window sizes. Provide an isolated demo launcher
so the checklist can safely create and clear its own sample data.

Include failed commands, unexecuted drafts and keyboard regression
checks to document the behaviours that this branch must preserve.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit window sizing to usable monitor bounds
commitResults.messageBody:
The unconditional 720 by 600 minimum can extend the window beyond a
small or scaled desktop, leaving part of the workspace off screen.

Keep the normal minimum where it fits, but cap each dimension at the
monitor's usable bounds. Clamp restored sizes and positions, and update
the limits when the window moves between monitors or returns from a
hidden or minimized state.

Add regression checks for restoration, monitor transitions and keyboard
access to both lists at reduced logical sizes. Update both manual guides
with the small-screen exception and separate physical scaling checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Unify class and student index styling
commitResults.messageBody:
Class and student indices use different typography, colours and gaps
before their names. This makes the same command-index information look
inconsistent across the two lists.

Give both card types a shared index style and define the spacing there
so future visual changes stay consistent. Preserve the existing names,
card content and interactions.

Check the rendered fonts, colours, padding and name offsets in the
workspace regression test, and add a matching manual check to both
guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align workspace columns with command index order
commitResults.messageBody:
Two-index commands expect STUDENT_INDEX before CLASS_INDEX, while the
workspace presents classes before students. The mismatch makes users
translate between command order and the visible layout.

Revise the earlier classes-first layout by placing Students on the left
and Classes on the right. Let keyboard traversal follow that visual
order and retain the adjustable split, slate theme and passive class
rows.

Update layout and keyboard regression checks and both branch-specific
manual guides, including navigation at reduced logical screen sizes.

Student cards retain row selection while Classes are passive. The
highlight suggests a row action even though commands use typed indices.

Reuse the existing read-only list for Students and show focus on the
list border, keeping keyboard, wheel and scrollbar navigation. Make End
reach the actual bottom so variable-height student cards stay readable.

Extend interaction checks to both lists, including mouse clicks, empty
lists and unchanged displayed data. Update the branch's manual guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show live header counts in aligned pills
commitResults.messageBody:
Counts share the section titles, making the headings harder to scan.
Separate them into matching slate-blue pills aligned to the right of
each header row so titles and counts are easier to distinguish.

Keep counts live and allow them to wrap within narrow panes. Update
layout assertions and manual guides to cover alignment and wrapping.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refine student and class card presentation
commitResults.messageBody:
Student details and class headings need a clearer visual hierarchy.
Keep the cards compact while making identities easier to distinguish.

Unify heading typography, align supporting details, and soften card
borders and tags. Use white indices and light blue module codes to
distinguish command references from class identity.

Retain readable wrapping and update card checks and manual guides
to cover the refined presentation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep class headings compact when wrapping
commitResults.messageBody:
Separate heading labels add sizing code and can make narrow cards
taller. Class headings should wrap as compactly as a single label.

Render module codes and class names in one wrapping heading while
preserving their colours. Remove duplicated size bindings and keep
row heights consistent so class scrolling remains reliable.

Cover repeated resizing and long module codes in regression tests,
and update both manual testing guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove personal UI testing guides and launchers
commitResults.messageBody:
The branch-specific guides and demo launchers are personal testing aids.
Keeping them in the shared repository adds material outside the product
and standard developer documentation.

Remove these files from the branch while retaining external local
copies for manual testing. Keep automated tests and the standard
project testing documentation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reveal complete final rows when scrolling
commitResults.messageBody:
Variable-height lists can use stale row measurements at the end.
This leaves the final student or class card outside the viewport on
Ubuntu, even when the same checks pass on macOS.

Measure destination rows before applying the final scroll position
for End and requests targeting the last row. Keep rows passive and
detach the new scroll handler when the skin is disposed.

Cover fractional row heights, small viewports and empty scroll requests.

Windows can restore a minimized window to its native monitor position.
The test assumes a move to a simulated secondary monitor survives that
restore, so it fails despite the monitor sizing checks passing.

Test minimized restoration by changing the current monitor's supplied
usable bounds instead. Keep geometry and minimum-size assertions, and
retain the visible-window monitor movement coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit restored windows after native size updates
commitResults.messageBody:
Windows can restore saved dimensions after JavaFX reports that a
window is no longer minimized. An immediate fit can be overwritten,
leaving the restored window larger than the usable screen.

Queue a screen-aware fit after restoration, including on the same
monitor, while keeping ordinary resizing unrestricted.

Simulate a late native size update in the restore regression without
depending on native minimize animations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show student totals and simplify card typography
commitResults.messageBody:
Student counts show only the displayed list size, making filtered
results harder to compare with the complete student collection.
Card details also use several font sizes and weights.

Show live displayed and total student counts in the existing pill.
Use one heading size and one regular detail size across both card
types so supporting information has a consistent visual hierarchy.

Update workspace checks for filtered and changing totals, shared
heading fonts, and regular detail fonts. All 871 tests pass on
JavaFX 17 and 25, alongside Checkstyle and coverage generation.

The data-file path is smaller than the surrounding supporting text.
Increase it to 12 pixels to improve readability and match card details.

All six workspace tests pass, including the scaled-screen layout checks.

Command syntax is available only after requesting help or submitting
an invalid command. Users need guidance while composing commands.

Add an always-visible hint strip beneath the input with syntax for all
18 commands, optional-argument notation and Enter reminders. Adapt the
reference layout and syntax lookup to the current parsers.

Keep typing limited to guidance updates and preserve Enter execution,
history navigation and existing errors without adding data previews.

Cover defaults, syntax, wrapping and typing without execution. Add
manual guides and verify independence from the usability changes.
All 898 tests pass on JavaFX 17 and 25; Checkstyle, coverage generation
and the JAR build pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align command hints with merged index syntax
commitResults.messageBody:
The merged assign and deleteclass commands identify displayed records
by index, while their hints still describe identity prefixes. Partial
command suggestions are also hard to distinguish from prose.

Update hints, parser-backed examples and manual guides to use the
implemented index syntax. Keep student deletion unchanged.

Separate command syntax from its reminder, using clear pipe separators
and brighter monospace text so similar command names are easier to read.
Preserve Enter-only execution and cover typing without data changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Emphasize the main command hint line
commitResults.messageBody:
Command names need stronger emphasis to stand apart from the quieter
Enter reminder and argument explanations.

Increase the monospace command line to 13 pixels and use bold weight.
Keep supporting guidance at 12 pixels and verify that both lines wrap
without clipping at narrow widths.

All 13 command-box and workspace tests pass on JavaFX 17 and 25, and
Checkstyle passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow selected punctuation in student names
commitResults.messageBody:
The name validator rejects ordinary names containing punctuation, and
slash input can conflict with command field prefixes.

Accept the agreed ASCII punctuation and convert backslashes after name
field extraction. Store forward slashes and accept either spelling in
searches. Keep command-input guidance separate from storage constraints
so each error describes the format accepted by its caller.

Add model and parser tests for accepted names, rejected characters, and
slash conversion. Retain the agreed rejection of Unicode names in #203.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover student name workflows and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Generated test commands insert stored slashes directly into name fields,
which the command parser rejects. Existing tests use plain names and do
not expose this mismatch or punctuation-sensitive search behavior.

Convert stored slashes back to command-input backslashes in test helpers
and cover generated add/edit commands, including prefix-like name text.

Verify canonical JSON names and storage error guidance. Exercise names
through editing, searching, restart, command history, class membership,
and attendance, and ensure rejected commands leave saved data unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document student name rules and testing
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides describe the old name restrictions and do not distinguish
command-input backslashes from forward slashes in stored JSON names.

Explain the accepted punctuation, slash conversion, validation messages,
and whole-word search behavior. Clarify the agreed ASCII-only scope of
issue #203 and add disposable manual tests for names and persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the student name issue reference
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide references #203, while the assigned student name
issue is #208. Point the documented scope to the assigned issue.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify module and class validation feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
Rejected module and class names can satisfy the character restrictions
listed in their error messages. The missing constraints leave users
without a clear correction.

Explain that module codes must start with a letter and class names need
at least one letter or digit. Include familiar module and class examples
in constraint and empty-field messages while preserving accepted inputs.

Cover the examples and numeric class names in parser tests for #221.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align command hints with documented syntax
commitResults.messageBody:
Hints use different parameter names from command usage and the User
Guide, making the same command appear to have different syntax.

Use INDEX for single-index commands and KEYWORD for find. Retain the
explicit student and class placeholders for commands taking both
indices.

Check the hints against accepted input and usage examples to prevent the
inconsistencies reported in #250 from recurring.

Generic errors hide the field, displayed-list bounds, or enforced
constraint that caused rejection. Unsupported prefixes can also be
reported as invalid values in otherwise valid fields.

Show current displayed ranges and empty-list recovery instructions.
Identify missing and unsupported fields, explain numeric limits, and
give corrective examples for empty edits, tags, and email constraints.
Include the unknown command and case-sensitivity guidance in its error.

Share prefix validation across the affected parsers and update existing
regression expectations. Preserve accepted values and business rules.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover command guidance across filtered views
commitResults.messageBody:
Message changes need verification through parsing, displayed selection,
and persistence together. Unit checks alone cannot confirm that rejected
commands leave filtered views and saved data unchanged.

Exercise unsupported and missing fields, filtered and empty index
ranges, threshold limits, and unknown commands through LogicManager.
Verify that rejections preserve records, memberships, history, filters,
and JSON data. Retain coverage for clearing tags with an empty edit
field.

The guides and parser diagrams need to match the revised hints,
validation phases, and actionable errors.

Update syntax, constraints, examples, shared error explanations, and
manual tests. Describe prefix validation and displayed-index recovery in
the Developer Guide and add a validation activity diagram. Update the
affected parser diagrams and correct documentation navigation links.

Verify the guides with the CI MarkBind version and inspect the rendered
diagrams alongside the passing application checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reveal both records after membership changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Assignment leaves the affected class off-screen, and membership changes
do not reveal the affected student.

Capture both targets before execution and locate them in the updated
views after success. Preserve active filters and avoid revealing a
replacement row when an unassigned record disappears from a view.

Cover successful reveals, rejected commands, typing, focus and filters
with workspace regression tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep student card wrapping stable while scrolling
commitResults.messageBody:
Student detail heights depend on a previous layout width. Recycled
cells can reserve too little space, allowing contact details to overlap
tags or neighbouring content.

Measure wrapped children at their proposed width and use the same row
calculation for layout. Remove the width-dependent height bindings.

Exercise repeated scrolling and resizing, optional-field edits and
